title: S3 lifecycle policies: automatic tiering

kcs.statement: An S3 lifecycle configuration holds rules, scoped to a bucket, prefix or tag, that move objects to cheaper storage classes after a set age; for example Standard to Standard-IA at 30 days, then to Glacier Deep Archive at 180.
Lifecycle expiration actions delete objects, or old noncurrent versions, after a set age, so logs and temporary data stop adding storage cost automatically.

problem_ideas: Given rules 'Standard-IA at 30 days, Deep Archive at 180, expire at 365', say where a 45-day-old, a 200-day-old and a 400-day-old object are.
Logs are read for 1 week, kept for audit for 1 year, then deleted: pick the transition and expiration actions that fit.
Apply a rule only to objects under the prefix 'raw/': what scopes the rule?
A versioned bucket keeps growing although users delete files: which lifecycle action fixes it?
Compute the monthly storage bill for 10 TB of logs with and without a 30-day transition to Standard-IA, given per-GB prices.
Which tool fits each need: lifecycle rule or Intelligent-Tiering, for a known versus an unknown access pattern?
